issues.legal_issue: A civil suit may set aside a revenue sale when the arrear for which the property was sold was not due.
material_facts: The owners’ actual land-revenue arrears when the sale was ordered were Rs. 730/13/-.
The sale proclamation stated that Rs. 1,354/9/- was due and that the property was being sold to recover that amount.
The owners challenged the sale in a civil suit on the ground that the stated arrear was not due.
issues.conclusion: The sale was invalid and had to be set aside because the arrear for which the property was sold was not due.
issues.legal_principle: Section 149(2) of the C.P. Land Revenue Act, 1917, permits a civil suit to set aside a sale on the ground that the arrear for which the property was sold was not due. Read with the Act’s revenue-sale scheme, including sections 143, 145, 146 and 149(1), the amount for which the property is sold must be stated accurately; a sale for an arrear that was not due is distinct from a challenge based on an irregularity or mistake. Rewa Mahton v. Ram Kishan Singh and Ram Prosad Choudhury v. Ram Jadu Lahiri were distinguished because they concerned different statutory provisions and sale procedures.

predicates.civil_suit_challenging_revenue_sale: An owner challenged a revenue sale by bringing a civil suit.
predicates.sale_proclamation_identified_specific_ar: The sale proclamation identified a specific arrear as the amount for which the property was being sold.
predicates.proclaimed_arrear_exceeded_arrear_then_d: The amount identified in the proclamation exceeded the arrear actually due when the sale was ordered.
predicates.sale_set_aside_for_arrear_not_due: The sale is set aside because the arrear for which the property was sold was not due.

issues.definition: When an owner brings a civil suit challenging a revenue sale and the proclamation identifies an arrear greater than the amount then due, the sale is set aside for an arrear not due.

issues.legal_issue: Arrears that accrue after a revenue sale is ordered and proclaimed cannot be added to the arrear specified for that sale to validate it without separate proceedings.
material_facts: The sale was ordered and proclaimed for an arrear of Rs. 730/13/-, but the proclamation stated a larger amount.
Further arrears accrued after the proclamation, bringing the total arrears to Rs. 1,354/9/- by the sale date.
The authorities proceeded with the sale for the larger amount without separately initiating proceedings for the subsequently accrued arrears.
issues.conclusion: The later-accruing arrears could not be counted to validate the sale; each specific arrear required separate proceedings, and the sale had to be set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 149(2) of the C.P. Land Revenue Act, 1917, the arrear for which a property is sold is the arrear determined when the sale is ordered and specified in the proclamation. The Act’s scheme requires each specific arrear to be dealt with separately, so arrears accruing after the sale order and proclamation cannot be added without following the prescribed procedure. Section 143 also contemplates payment of the arrear specified for the sale before the lot is knocked down, supporting the need for the amount to be correctly stated.

rule.if: civil_suit_challenging_revenue_sale and sale_arrear_fixed_before_proclamation and later_arrears_added_to_sale_amount and later_arrears_not_separately_processed

predicates.civil_suit_challenging_revenue_sale: An owner challenged a revenue sale by bringing a civil suit.
predicates.sale_arrear_fixed_before_proclamation: The arrear for the sale was determined before the sale proclamation was issued.
predicates.later_arrears_added_to_sale_amount: Arrears that accrued after the proclamation were included in the amount used to justify the sale.
predicates.later_arrears_not_separately_processed: The authorities did not separately process the later-accruing arrears before including them in the sale amount.
predicates.later_arrears_do_not_validate_sale: Later-accruing arrears do not validate a sale conducted for an amount that was not separately proceeded against.

issues.definition: If later-accruing arrears are added to a previously fixed sale amount without separate processing, they do not validate the sale.
